perplexity.description:
Killer Watts is a 1980 double-LP compilation album released by Epic Records, featuring a diverse roster of artists under the label. The album showcases a broad spectrum of rock styles, from hard rock and new wave to pop and blues-inflected tracks, reflecting the eclectic tastes and trends of the era. Recorded at the Automatt studio, the compilation highlights the production quality and sonic experimentation characteristic of late 1970s and early 1980s rock, with each artist contributing a distinct flavor to the overall collection.

As a compilation, Killer Watts does not represent a single artist’s discography but rather serves as a snapshot of Epic Records’ rock-oriented roster at the time. It was not the label’s first such compilation, but it stands out for its ambitious two-LP format and the inclusion of both established and emerging acts. The album’s release in 1980 positioned it as a companion to the evolving rock landscape, capturing the energy and diversity of the period.

While Killer Watts did not achieve major commercial success or widespread critical acclaim, it remains a notable artifact for collectors and fans of early 1980s rock. Its value lies in its curation and the opportunity it provides to hear a range of artists in a single, cohesive package, making it a representative example of the era’s compilation albums.
